I farm 6 mu here in Quzhou. It is not much land but it feeds the family and my wife and I work it ourselves. The kids help when they come back. Two of them work in town now.

I do wheat in winter and maize in summer like everyone here. That is how we have always done it. My neighbor Old Wang gets good harvests so I watch what he puts down and I do about the same.

For the wheat I put one bag of compound fertilizer when I plow — that is 50 jin per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the shop in town. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up and starts growing tall, I spread urea, about half a bag per mu, maybe 25 jin. If I put less my wheat looks yellow and thin and I lose harvest. Better to put a bit extra. Fertilizer costs money but losing the harvest costs more.

For maize it is the same idea. One bag compound when I seed, then urea when the maize is knee-high. Maize eats a lot, everybody knows this.

Water — I have my own well so I can pump. Wheat needs water in winter before freeze, then in spring when it comes up, then when the ear is filling. Three or four times. Maize drinks a lot in July when it is tasseling, I water twice usually, more if no rain.

I spray two times each crop. Once for weeds, once for bugs. Sometimes the wheat gets that yellow rust and I spray again but I try not to because the spray is expensive.

Seeds I buy from the shop — for maize the hybrid seeds, everyone uses those now, you cannot save your own or it does not grow well. Wheat I get improved seed too, the shop owner tells me which is good this year.

For the wheat I plow with rotary after maize comes off. For maize I just seed straight into the wheat stubble — saves time and the ground stays moist.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 jin per mu, maize about 550. If the weather is okay I expect similar this year.
